data.one_liner: Dynamic light and dark theme switching with persistence for Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Allows apps to dynamically switch between light, dark, and system-default themes. Persists theme choices across app restarts using shared_preferences and provides listeners for theme changes.
use_when: You need to support manual light and dark theme switching in your app.
You want theme mode changes to persist automatically across app restarts.
You want to support system-adaptive theme changes easily.
avoid_when: You only need a static theme defined once without any runtime switching or persistence.
You are using a complex custom state management setup where you prefer handling theme state manually.
strengths: Persists theme mode automatically across app restarts.
Supports both Material (MaterialApp) and Cupertino (CupertinoApp) apps.
Includes a debug floating theme button for quick testing.
Provides ValueNotifier to easily listen to theme changes.
weaknesses: Does not persist full custom theme data changes, only the theme mode (light/dark/system).
Requires wrapping the app root widget.
data.setup_notes: Wrap your MaterialApp or CupertinoApp with AdaptiveTheme or CupertinoAdaptiveTheme.

alternatives.name: flex_color_scheme
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you need advanced custom Material color schemes and extensive pre-built themes rather than just light/dark toggling.

data.minimal_example:
AdaptiveTheme(
  light: ThemeData.light(useMaterial3: true),
  dark: ThemeData.dark(useMaterial3: true),
  initial: AdaptiveThemeMode.light,
  builder: (theme, darkTheme) => MaterialApp(
    title: 'Adaptive Theme Demo',
    theme: theme,
    darkTheme: darkTheme,
    home: MyHomePage(),
  ),
)
